subject: Post-call: Multilingual model evals & next steps (EU / APAC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Dubois <sophie.dubois@globexretail.eu>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@apaccommerce.co.jp>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Multilingual model evals & next steps (EU / APAC)

Hi Sophie, Hiro — great to meet today. Thanks for walking through the Globex Retail use cases (customer support triage + assisted response). Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

What we heard:
- Primary requirement: high-quality responses in French, German, Spanish (EU), and Japanese/Korean (APAC) for both short answer and multi-turn context.
- Latency SLO target: p95 < 350ms for short responses; throughput needs are modest initially (pilot volume ~50k messages/month) but expected to grow if pilot succeeds.
- Risk areas: formal vs. informal address (German Sie/Tu), Spanish regional variants (ES vs LATAM), and honorific/politeness in Japanese.

Immediate next steps (owner / timeline):
1) Redwood: share recommended models, evaluation artifacts (prompt sets + benchmarks) and a short runbook for locale-specific checks — by EOD Tue (see attachments & Drive link). (marissa)
2) Globex: share a 1-week sample of anonymized transcripts per locale and any hard constraints on PII retention / residency. (sophie)
3) Joint: schedule a 45-min technical review with your MLops and our runtime team to discuss quantization/latency tradeoffs. Proposed times: Wed or Thu next week.

Model & eval preview (high level):
- Recommended starting variants: RW-7B-quant (low cost, strong on short responses), Redwood-XL-13B (better multi-turn coherence for assisted responses).
- Suggested inference config: int8/quantization for non-PII data; use dynamic KV cache and 512-token max for context to balance latency.
- We'll run locale-specific evals: automatic metrics + human preference tests focusing on politeness/formality, entity preservation, and diacritic handling.

Links & attachments: prompt sets (CSV), latest multilingual bench PDF, and a Drive folder with per-locale test cases. DocuSign for the pilot SOW will follow via procurement.

Questions for you: can you confirm whether Globex requires EU-only hosting for EU customer messages? Also please share sample transcripts when ready (Sophie).

I'll follow up with the benchmark links and the prompt set in the next email.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual model evals & next steps (EU / APAC)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few things from our side: 

- We can provide anonymized transcripts for FR/DE/ES and JP by end of day Thurs. Will redaction be sufficient or do you need a particular schema?
- EU-only hosting: for the pilot we prefer EU residency for EU customer content. We'll need to confirm with procurement on APAC residency requirements.
- Latency: p95 <350ms is our target for chat; for background async tasks higher latency is ok.

Also can you call out expected token/unit costs for the two recommended model families and whether Redwood Dedicated is recommended for predictable latency if we scale? Lastly — curious about quantized int8 fidelity on special characters/diacritics (we've had regressions before with other vendors).

Happy to book a technical review Wed 10:00-11:00 CET if that works for your eng team.

Best,
Sophie
Head of Digital Experience, Globex Retail
Sophie.dubois@globexretail.eu

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Dubois <sophie.dubois@globexretail.eu>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@apaccommerce.co.jp>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual model evals & next steps (EU / APAC)

Thanks Sophie — great. A few concrete items in response: 

1) Redaction/schema: redacted transcripts are fine; a simple replace for emails/phone numbers and a mapping table for user IDs works. We have a short redaction template we can share if helpful.

2) Residency: we can run EU-only pilot on our EU-hosted cluster (Private control plane + EU region). If you need hard guarantees for the pilot we can document the deployment topology in the SOW. (Vivek, Neha — noting for provisioning).

3) Cost/latency notes: 
- RW-7B-quant: estimated ~0.6x cost of 13B float variants; p95 latency for single-request short responses typically ~180-300ms on our hosted fleet with batching disabled.
- Redwood-XL-13B: higher quality for multi-turn; p95 ~270-420ms depending on context length.
- Dedicated: recommended when you need predictable sub-300ms p95 at scale; for pilot we'll run hosted EU cluster.

4) Quantization & diacritics: we will run targeted regression tests. Known failure modes: tokenization splits and byte-level fallback can degrade accent handling in some Spanish/Portuguese datasets; Japanese politeness forms need evaluation on suffix patterns rather than single-token checks. We'll include human raters for FR/DE/ES/JP/KO to validate pragmatics and formality.

5) Attachments & links (all in Drive):
- Prompt set: 20270530_prompt_set_v2.csv — per-locale prompts + expected behaviors + do-not-respond examples.
- Bench PDF: multilingual_bench_results_20270529.pdf — aggregate scores (BLEU/SacreBLEU, chrF, and human preference %). Note: we emphasize human preference over BLEU for these tasks.
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcDEFghIJ (per-locale test cases, human eval rubric).

Would you like us to spin up an evaluation run against your sample transcripts as soon as you provide them? We can deliver a one-page summary plus a jitter plot of errors by locale in 3 business days.

If Wed 10:00 CET works, I'll book the technical review and loop in our infra lead (Rishi) and quantization engineer.

Thanks — talk soon.
Marissa
